description: Kotlin Multiplatform network stack: QUIC v1/v2 (RFC 9000/9001/9002/9369), HTTP/3 with QPACK, TLS 1.3 over OpenSSL 3.5, and Ktor client and server engines, for the JVM, Android, Kotlin/Native Linux, Apple (macOS, iOS) and Windows.
rules: Kuicksilver is 0.x and experimental: the API can change between any two 0.x releases; docs/stability.md says which API is stable and which is experimental.
Use the same version for every io.kuicksilver artifact; each module depends only on the layer directly below it (native, tls, quic, http3, then the Ktor engines).

For Ktor, use HttpClient(Kuicksilver) for the client and embeddedServer(Kuicksilver) for the server; the client starts on HTTP/1.1 over TLS and moves to HTTP/3 after the server announces it with Alt-Svc, unless configured otherwise.
OpenSSL 3.5 is statically linked inside kuicksilver-native; no system OpenSSL is needed or used. The library is not FIPS-certified.
0-RTT is opt-in and experimental (off by default); BBR is opt-in and experimental, CUBIC is the default congestion controller.
loops > 1 works only on Linux and Android; macOS, iOS and Windows run one loop per port.
JS and Wasm are not targets; HTTP/2, HTTP/3 server push and WebTransport are not supported.
